data.text: Implementation pushed as 88edfc5c to PR #129. Fixed-window preflight checks each occupied or vacant key in input order, uses fail-closed quota arithmetic, and lazily counts projected insertions. A private preflighted owner retains the original locks and checks into commit. The map entry API lets commit reuse a vacant or expired slot. Release Runlimit tests pass, including denial with a corrupt late counter and no prefix charge. Seven compile diagnostics confirm premature commit, proof forgery, check substitution and four foreign configuration calls are rejected. Production trace probes match master across 384,000 fixed-window operations and a further 30,000 operations per algorithm. One hundred 8-thread rounds (76,800 calls) found exact accounting. Local full verification, hosted checks and PR-wide review in progress.

Final PR #129 head aa3e3ef0 passed complete pinned Rust 1.100.0 verification on macOS arm64 with two Rust test threads and in hosted Linux CI (https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/actions/runs/45861638570). Hosted native Runlimit PostgreSQL, macOS subprocess, verified-tree and repository policy checks passed. The clean full-PR code review followed a repair that narrowed single-check outcomes to enforced or shadow denials and GCRA arithmetic failures to quota-only denials. Nine negative compile probes passed. Release crate tests passed, 384,000 fixed-window operations and 30,000 per-backend trace operations matched master, and 76,800 contending calls reconciled exactly. A warmed 4,096-key late denial allocated 0 bytes under lock compared with 576 KiB on the previous PR. Median one-shard warmed allowed lock time was 54.8 microseconds versus 70.1 on master and 123.3 on the previous PR. Eight-caller warmed p99 was 3.29 ms versus 3.91 ms on master. Synthetic same-process measurements against master showed about 1% longer whole calls for 16-shard cold insertion and simultaneous expiry, around 7 ns extra per warmed single check and about 5% on warmed 32- and 4,096-key GCRA batches. The PR description includes the measurements and verification links. GitHub reports the PR mergeable with zero review threads.

fields.description:
## Finding
runlimit-postgres carries three copies of the limiter shell (pool, config, observer, Debug, migrate, guarded bounded connection) in src/lib.rs, src/gcra.rs and src/attempts.rs, and they have drifted: PostgresAttemptLimiter::migrate clones ATTEMPTS_MIGRATOR.migrations and always retires its connection while the other two re-invoke sqlx::migrate! and reuse it on success; PostgresLimiter's Debug uses finish_non_exhaustive, PostgresGcraLimiter's finish, and PostgresAttemptLimiter has neither Debug nor config(). CheckTransaction refreshes SET LOCAL timeouts before every statement and commit, while maintenance.rs exposes raw helpers that gcra::cleanup_transaction must pair by hand three times. The authoritative-elapsed subtraction exists in admission.rs and gcra/response.rs. tests/postgres.rs, tests/gcra.rs and tests/attempts.rs each reimplement the disposable-schema harness and the XOR shard-key helper.

## Remediation
One private limiter base owning pool, config, observer, Debug, migration and bounded guarded connections; one bounded transaction generic over the check and maintenance families that refreshes timeouts itself; one pending-response finisher; one shared live-test schema fixture.

## Public surface
Additive only: PostgresAttemptLimiter gains Debug and config(), and new becomes const. No hard cut. Behaviour notes belong in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

Related: batter-ctk7.12 (connection disposition classifier) builds on the single transaction and guard this leaves behind.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The three limiters share one private base for pool, config, observer, Debug, migrate and bounded connection acquisition; one transaction type refreshes server timeouts before every statement and commit for checks and cleanup; one function subtracts authoritative elapsed time for both quota limiters; the three live suites use one schema fixture; scripts/verify.sh and the live runlimit-postgres suites pass.

## Finding (pre-existing; raised by Codex review of PR #130, not introduced there)
In runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/transaction.rs, BoundedTransaction::execute, fetch_all and fetch_one refresh the server timeouts and then pass the statement to before_commit, which wraps it in timeout_at(deadline, ..). The remaining budget is checked when the refresh is computed (protocol::remaining_server_timeout_settings) but not again after the refresh returns. If the refresh starts within budget and its response arrives at or after the deadline, the statement is still polled: Tokio polls the wrapped future before the timer, so the SQL is sent, the client timer then fires, and an otherwise reusable connection is retired (ConnectionOutcome::MustClose) for a statement that could only time out. Only the commit path re-checks (attempt_commit).

The same sequence existed before the shared transaction: CheckTransaction::prepare followed by check_before_commit in admission.rs, and set_maintenance_server_timeouts followed by maintenance_before_commit in maintenance.rs and gcra.rs (base aa3e3ef0).

## Proposed remediation
Check the deadline at entry to before_commit and return a reusable pre-commit timeout without polling the step, covered by a poll-recording future as attempt_commit is. This is a runtime break under the repository rule: a statement that today finishes inside the client timer's slack, and with it a denial the check would have returned, becomes TimedOutBeforeCommit. It needs a Breaking CHANGELOG entry with before/after handling and log text for check, check_all, admit and cleanup.

## Related
batter-2oht (shared transaction), batter-ctk7.12 (single connection-disposition classifier).
fields.acceptance_criteria: No pre-commit statement is polled once the operation deadline has been reached, proven by a poll-recording unit test for both families; the connection stays reusable in that case; the runtime break is recorded in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after handling and log text; live runlimit-postgres suites pass.
fields.title: runlimit-postgres sends a pre-commit statement after its timeout refresh used up the operation deadline

data.text: Correction to the description: the statement that follows an over-budget refresh is not certain to time out. Tokio polls the statement before the timer, so a ready database result can win and the call can still return (for example a denial on the last preflight). The connection is retired only when the client timer fires first.

fields.description:
PostgresAttemptLimiter samples pg_catalog.clock_timestamp() for every evaluation and writes nothing when an admission is denied or a completion or claim is stale. The shared AttemptState contract (runlimit-core) lets a backend skip storing the settled state only while its evaluation instants never decrease. A wall clock can step backwards (clock correction, failover to a primary whose clock is behind).

Consequence, unchanged since the attempt protocol was introduced and pinned by the live test a_backwards_clock_step_revives_an_unreplaced_expired_lease in runlimit-postgres/tests/attempt_state.rs: after admission has reported Backoff for an expired lease, or a completion has reported Stale for it, a clock step behind the lease deadline makes that lease live again until the deadline. Admission then reports Busy instead of Backoff, and the lease's own outstanding receipt can complete; a Success resets the failure the earlier denial reported.

Why it was not fixed in PR #131 (batter-ctk7.8): a first attempt stored the expiry inside the denying admission. Review found that incomplete in three ways: the denial is still reported when that commit fails or is unacknowledged; standalone complete, claim_in, finish_in and complete_in observe the same expiry and store nothing, and low_level callers must roll back on Stale by contract, so the seam cannot store it at all; and it made denials commit the bounded cleanup batch, changing shard capacity behavior between releases. Storing each observation cannot cover the seam.

Proposed direction (unexecuted): evaluate attempts against a nondecreasing instant, as PostgreSQL GCRA does with its shard watermark, so the contract's precondition holds for every path including the low-level seam. That needs a forward migration and a mixed-version rollout plan.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Every PostgreSQL attempt path (admit, complete, low_level claim_in/finish_in/complete_in) evaluates against an instant that never decreases for a subject, or the contract is otherwise met on every path. A live test steps the server clock backwards after each kind of observation and shows the lease stays expired. Mixed-version behavior and any migration are documented with a Breaking entry where a previously succeeding call now fails.

data.text: PR review loop (2026-11-27), PR #131. Round 1 (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh): 3 P2 + 1 P3. Round 2: 5 findings, all on that stored expiry (denial reported when its commit fails; standalone complete and the low-level seam store nothing; unchecked UPDATE row count; committed cleanup changes shard capacity across releases; unmarked run-time break). Decision: back the stored expiry out in a59a2549, because storing per observation cannot cover low_level callers that must roll back on Stale. PostgreSQL's clock-step behavior is unchanged from earlier releases, now documented (AttemptState obligations, module docs, README, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG) and pinned by live test a_backwards_clock_step_revives_an_unreplaced_expired_lease. ## Finding (memory counterpart of batter-2oht; duplicated, drifted)
On origin/master (bc1957a5) `MemoryStore` and `GcraStore` still carry two copies of the same public shell: `new`, `builder`, the `MemoryStoreBuilder`/`GcraStoreBuilder` types with `with_clock` and `build`, `with_observer`, `stats`, `clear`, `recover_poisoned`, and `Debug`. PR #129 (batter-ctk7.10) shared the shard session and batch preflight-to-commit but left this shell duplicated.

The copies have already drifted:
- `Debug` for `MemoryStore` renders `shard_state: [REDACTED]` through a private `Redacted` type (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/store.rs:190), while `GcraStore` passes `&"[REDACTED]"`, which renders the quoted string `"[REDACTED]"` (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs:160).
- The `with_observer` rustdoc on `MemoryStore` states the after-unlock and panic-isolation contract; the `GcraStore` copy omits it.

## Remediation
One private store base, generic over the entry type, that owns config, clock, shards, observer, the redacted `Debug` body and the stats/clear/recover delegation, wrapped by both public stores. Keep both public types and builders; no hard cut is required. Pin identical `Debug` output for both stores in a test.

## Public surface
Additive or behaviour-only: `GcraStore`'s `Debug` text changes from `"[REDACTED]"` to `[REDACTED]`. Record it in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md. It is not a compile break; note it in case anything matches that text.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- `MemoryStore` and `GcraStore` share one private implementation of their construction, observer, Debug and stats/clear/recover plumbing; neither file contains a second copy.
- A test asserts both stores render `shard_state: [REDACTED]` without quotes and without counter state.
- No public item removed or renamed; public-API surface diff recorded; CHANGELOG notes the GcraStore Debug text change.
- runlimit-memory file budgets do not grow; `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes and is recorded here.
fields.title: Share one MemoryStore/GcraStore public shell and pin identical redacted Debug output

fields.description:
## Finding (persistent protocol derived twice in Rust, untested against SQL)
`protocol::capacity_shard` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/protocol.rs:304) is the single Rust derivation of the persistent capacity shard and has a golden vector (`capacity_shard_protocol_has_a_golden_vector`). The attempt admission path re-derives it inline as `i16::from(fingerprint[0] ^ subject[0])` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:226 on origin/master bc1957a5; :235 on PR #130; :255 on PR #131) with no golden vector. The attempts migration derives it a third time as the generated `capacity_shard` column (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/attempts-migrations). runlimit/AGENTS.md requires one derivation per value and a shard derivation that stays stable across rolling deployment; nothing ties the inline Rust copy or the attempts SQL column to the protected one.

batter-2oht / PR #130 consolidates only the test-side XOR helper (`tests/support/mod.rs::capacity_shard_for`); PR #131 rewrites attempts.rs and keeps the inline expression.

## Remediation
Route attempt admission through `protocol::capacity_shard` (or one sibling accepting the attempt fingerprint and subject, under the same golden vector). Add a live test that the Rust-derived shard equals the stored generated `capacity_shard` column for attempt rows, as fixed-window and GCRA tests already do for their tables. Never change the derivation or rewrite the published migration.

Sequence after PR #131 (and PR #130) land, since both rewrite runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- runlimit-postgres production code contains exactly one Rust capacity-shard derivation, covered by the existing golden vector.
- A live PostgreSQL test proves the Rust derivation matches the attempts table's generated `capacity_shard` for multiple subjects and policies.
- No migration rewritten; persisted shard values unchanged.
- `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes and the ignored live suite outcome is recorded here.
fields.title: Derive the attempt capacity shard through protocol::capacity_shard and test it against the generated column
